answer: Cross-Epoch Reputation Signal Locking. Each identity's behavioral fingerprint (action timing, task mix, counterparty graph) is scored per epoch; the score becomes a weighted signal that only carries forward if the next epoch's fingerprint stays within a drift threshold. Sudden identity splits leave a mesa of inconsistent profiles that fail the cross-epoch check, so spawned sybils cannot harbor accumulated trust. An attacker must sustain plausible behavior across many epochs on every clone, multiplying operational cost linearly with each fake identity.
